About IMC

A global lens on finance.

IMC brings together students interested in finance, economics, politics, and international affairs. Through public education, market discussions, professional events, and applied research, members learn to connect global developments with companies, commodities, supply chains, and portfolios.

Our programming is designed for students at every level. Curiosity and critical thinking matter more than prior technical experience.

Meet the Executive Board
Club Structure

Three ways to engage with IMC.

Members can participate through open programming, the selective Analyst Program, or leadership on the Executive Board.

General Members

Access weekly education sessions, speaker events, and analyst portfolio updates.

Receive priority consideration during the Analyst Program application cycle.

Learn from analysts and ask questions about their investment research and portfolio updates.

Analyst Program

Designed for students who demonstrate a strong interest in international markets and a commitment to IMC.

Admission follows an application and interview process.

Receive advanced technical training and mentorship from experienced members.

Work in teams of three to track a portfolio spanning companies and markets around the world.

Executive Board

Oversee recruiting, speaker events, club operations, and industry relationships.

Lead meetings and events that give members practical knowledge and exposure to career opportunities.

Mentor members as they apply their interest in international markets to academics and recruiting.

Course Schedule & Location

Fall education sessions.

Our public curriculum develops a practical foundation in accounting, finance, valuation, portfolio construction, and global market analysis.

September 29

Accounting Fundamentals I

Balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement, and the relationship between the three financial statements.

Fulton 415
October 6

Accounting Fundamentals II

Financial statement linkages, working capital, non-cash items, depreciation and amortization, and accounting adjustments.

Fulton 415
October 13

Investment Fundamentals

Overview of equities, fixed income, commodities, currencies, and alternative assets, with an introduction to international markets.

Virtual
October 20

Portfolio Construction

Asset allocation, diversification, correlation, risk and return tradeoffs, and constructing portfolios across asset classes and geographies.

Fulton 511
October 27

Finance Fundamentals

Time value of money, discount rates, capital structure, cost of capital, and foundational corporate finance concepts.

Fulton 511
November 3

Review & Practice*

Review of accounting and finance concepts through technical exercises and case applications.

Fulton 415
November 10

Valuation & Modeling

Trading comparables, precedent transactions, valuation multiples, peer selection, free cash flow forecasting, and calculating enterprise value.

Fulton 511
November 17

DCF Valuation

Calculating terminal value, discounting, and calculating enterprise value and implied equity value.

Fulton 511
November 24

DCF Practice Day*

Reserved exclusively for Analyst Program members.

Fulton 415
December 1

DCF Valuation II*

Advanced DCF analysis, sensitivity tables, scenario analysis, valuation drivers, and implied valuation ranges.

Stokes S295
December 8

Geopolitical Risk & News Analysis

Assessing geopolitical events, supply-chain exposure, regulatory risks, and incorporating news catalysts into investment theses.

Fulton 511
